title: Comparing: longer, heavier, fuller
summary: Which is longer? Which is heavier? Measure with paper clips, hand spans and cups.
guide: To compare two things, line up their starts. Then see whose end goes further.
Look at the balance. The heavier pan goes down. The lighter pan goes up.
We can also measure with paper clips, hand spans or cups. These are {{term:non-standard-unit}}s.
Put the clips end to end. No gaps. No overlaps.

which-longer.title: Which is longer?
which-longer.prompt: Look at the pencil and the ribbon. Which is longer? Careful: they do not start in the same place.
which-longer.hint: The ribbon starts further along. Imagine sliding the ribbon back so it starts where the pencil starts.
which-longer.success: Well done! The pencil is longer. The ribbon just starts further along.
which-longer.why: The ribbon's end goes further. So why is the ribbon not longer?
which-longer.model: Because the ribbon starts in a different place. To compare, we must line up the starts. If we slide the ribbon back to start where the pencil starts, the pencil's end goes further.

feedback.wrong: The ribbon's end is further along because it starts further along. Line up the starts in your head.

which-heavier.title: Which is heavier?
which-heavier.prompt: Look at the balance. Is the melon heavier, or the three apples?
which-heavier.hint: Which pan has gone down? The heavier thing pulls its pan down.
which-heavier.success: Well done! The melon's pan is down, so the melon is heavier.
which-heavier.why: How do you know the melon is heavier?
which-heavier.model: The melon's pan has gone down. The heavier thing pulls its pan down. The lighter pan goes up.

feedback.wrong: The apples' pan is up. The lighter pan goes up, not the heavier one.

clips-pencil.title: How many clips long?
clips-pencil.prompt: First estimate: how many paper clips long is the pencil? Now put clips end to end until you reach the end of the pencil.
clips-pencil.hint: Press + to add a clip. Stop when the clips reach the end of the pencil.
clips-pencil.success: Well done! The pencil is 6 clips long.
clips-pencil.why: Why must the clips go end to end, with no gaps?
clips-pencil.model: If we leave gaps, we do not count the empty spaces. If the clips overlap, we count some places twice. So the clips must touch, end to end.

feedback.too-big: The clips go past the end of the pencil. Take one away.
feedback.too-small: The clips do not reach the end of the pencil yet. Add another.

spans-book.title: How many hand spans?
spans-book.prompt: Ali measures the book with his hand span. Add spans until you reach the end of the book.
spans-book.hint: Press + to add a span. Go to the end of the book.
spans-book.success: Well done! The book is 3 of Ali's spans.
spans-book.why: Sara's hand is bigger than Ali's. Would she measure more spans or fewer? Why?
spans-book.model: Fewer. Sara's span is bigger, so fewer spans reach the end of the book. That is why people get different numbers when they measure with hand spans.

feedback.too-big: The spans go past the end of the book. Take one away.
feedback.too-small: The spans do not reach the end of the book yet. Add another.

cups-jug.title: 4 cups of water
cups-jug.prompt: Maryam pours 4 cups of water into the jug. You pour 4 cups too.
cups-jug.hint: Each time you press +, you pour in one cup. Count to 4.
cups-jug.success: Well done! There are 4 cups of water in the jug.
cups-jug.why: Reza uses a smaller cup. Does he need more cups or fewer to fill the same jug?
cups-jug.model: More. A small cup holds less water, so Reza has to pour more cups.

feedback.too-big: Too much water. Pour one cup out.
feedback.too-small: Not enough water. Pour in another cup.
